title: A new approach for credit card fraud detection using artificial bee colony optimization with ABC-based sampling method
authors: Darwish, A.; Elshewey, M. A.; Tarek, Z.
tldr: A novel ABC-based data sampling technique combined with Particle Swarm Optimization feature selection and Artificial Bee Colony-based classification achieved 98.78 percent accuracy and 0.996 AUC-ROC on the Kaggle credit card fraud dataset.
problem_and_motivation: Credit card fraud detection remains a critical challenge due to highly imbalanced datasets where fraudulent transactions are rare. Existing methods suffer from performance degradation on minority class instances and lack optimal feature selection mechanisms. There is a need for a comprehensive approach that addresses data imbalance, feature selection, and classification simultaneously using swarm intelligence.
approach: Developed an ABC-based sampling technique to address class imbalance by generating synthetic minority class instances using the Artificial Bee Colony algorithm.
Implemented PSO-based feature selection to identify the most discriminating features from the 30 available transaction attributes.
Built an ABC-based classifier that leverages the optimized feature subset for final fraud detection.
Tested the approach on the Kaggle credit card fraud detection dataset containing 284,807 transactions with 492 fraudulent cases.
Evaluated performance using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics across multiple experimental configurations.
findings: The proposed method achieved 98.78 percent accuracy and 0.996 AUC-ROC, outperforming existing approaches.
ABC-based sampling effectively addressed class imbalance, improving minority class detection rates.
PSO-based feature selection reduced dimensionality while maintaining or improving classification performance.
The combination of sampling, feature selection, and classification in a unified framework produced superior results compared to individual components.
The method demonstrated robustness across different class distributions and threshold settings.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a novel unified framework that integrates ABC-based data sampling, PSO-based feature selection, and ABC-based classification for credit card fraud detection. The key innovation is the ABC-based sampling technique that generates synthetic minority class instances while preserving the underlying data distribution, which outperforms SMOTE and other traditional sampling methods. The combined approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the benchmark Kaggle credit card fraud dataset.
directly_justifies: ABC-based sampling effectively addresses class imbalance in fraud detection datasets.
PSO-based feature selection identifies the most discriminating transaction attributes.
The unified framework achieves 98.78 percent accuracy and 0.996 AUC-ROC on benchmark data.
limits: Single dataset evaluation limits generalizability claims.
Computational cost of swarm intelligence methods may be prohibitive for real-time applications.
The method does not account for concept drift in evolving fraud patterns.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domains 8.A and 8.B are highly relevant as the paper's core contribution is anomaly detection for credit card fraud using novel swarm intelligence algorithms. Domain 6.A is medium relevance due to the predictive classification component. Domains 1-5, 7, 9-14 were considered and rejected: the paper does not address Filipino demographics, budgeting, banking design, trust, engagement, savings, debt, gambling, or synthetic data. The paper is focused purely on fraud detection algorithm development.

limitations: Evaluation limited to a single benchmark dataset.
Swarm intelligence methods may have high computational overhead for real-time deployment.
Does not address concept drift or evolving fraud patterns over time.
remember_this: ABC-based sampling outperforms SMOTE for addressing class imbalance in fraud detection.
PSO feature selection reduces dimensionality while maintaining classification accuracy.
